proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived whole-parent finite honesty, adaptive width order, regular Gaussian expected-length efficiency, local joint laws and matched lower orders on a lawful witness family. The mathematics and all cited nodes passed, but the delivered narrow specialization achieved incremental novelty against the field floor; constant-only recalibration cannot close the framework gap. The run stops before Lean formalization; a future broader re-anchor must beat the B=792 projection baseline and address the approximately 2.5e23 transition scale.
tldr: Binary treatments can change features beyond the mean, including outcome variance, as motivated by Martinez-Taboada--Ramdas--Kennedy. The prospective decision here compares which intervention arm has the more asymmetric counterfactual outcome distribution around its own intervention mean; a mean-only analysis can miss unequal upper- and lower-tail behavior. In the stipulated bounded two-stratum observational model, the reflection-discrepancy contrast admits one total connected interval with every-sample-size whole-parent honesty and signal-adaptive expected length, with matching lower orders on a confounded Legendre family and at an all-uniform law. Corrected joint Hilbert scores retain shared-record covariance in regular and quadratic laws. This assembled baseline is incremental. A prospective extension of the published distributional-treatment-effect setting and of \texttt{symmetry::symmetry\_test()} needs one interval that remains valid near reflection symmetry and gives regular precision when the contrast is separated from zero, supporting a materiality threshold decision. Field relevance requires resolving the finite-to-efficient open question as a theorem: explicit finite calibration retaining whole-parent \(0.90\) honesty, the regular Gaussian expected-length constant, and a strict quantitative width improvement over \(C\) on the observable positive Legendre subfamily. An applied deployment is not established.
gap: Direct-sample unknown-center symmetry and causal Hilbert inference are established separately. The assembled finite original-record reflection-contrast benchmark is incremental. Martinez-Taboada--Ramdas--Kennedy, Section 1, motivates binary-treatment distributional analysis because treatment can change features beyond the mean, including variance. Its distribution-equality test does not study reflection asymmetry or the interval here. Wornbard et al. provides null-calibrated residual-HSIC inference and alternative-regime efficient intervals, and explicitly leaves non-asymptotic theory open. The question here is one finite-honest causal-reflection interval attaining the regular Gaussian expected-length constant.
fill: The core specifies a total empirical interval, conservative constants, lawful likelihood witnesses, corrected joint scores and local-law obligations. The baseline has an incremental ceiling. Field relevance is conditional on an affirmative finite-to-efficient theorem giving explicit calibration with whole-parent \(0.90\) honesty, the regular Gaussian expected-length constant, and a public \(C_{\mathrm L}<C\) width guarantee on the named observable positive Legendre subfamily, as required by the open-ended question.
